Summary: Jesus' church-discipline command: if your brother trespasses against you, go and tell him his fault between you and him alone, before taking witnesses or telling the church.
Commandment: Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.
Application: Distinct from the forgiveness command (live row), which governs the heart toward an offender, this governs the process: private first, then witnesses, then the church — gaining the brother, not winning the case.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: 'if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother' (Matthew 18:15).
Function: Go to him alone first — before witnesses, before the church. Not Mosaic law but a New Testament command — the threefold division does not sort it. Its goal was to gain the brother, not to win the case: if he hears you, thou hast gained thy brother. The evil it addressed was public accusation as a first resort, which hardens wrong into a feud. It restrained that evil by ordering the process: private first, then witnesses, then the church — each step aimed at restoration, not exposure.
